title: Trace, Replay & Dry Runs
objective: After this lesson you will be able to emit structured traces with spans, replay runs deterministically (seeded randomness, recorded tools), dry-run without side effects, and time-travel from checkpoints.
why: 'Works on my run' ends debugging before it starts: unlogged inputs, unseeded randomness, and live side effects make agent failures unreproducible by construction. Deterministic replay (same inputs + seed → identical trace), dry-run sandboxes (full logic, stubbed effects), and time-travel forks (resume from any checkpoint) convert mysteries into measurements.

blocks.text: Every run records: **inputs** (full state + versions), **seed** (all randomness derived), **spans** (per node/tool with timing + verdicts), **tool responses** (recorded verbatim). Same inputs + seed replays identically — proven by test, not assumed. Unseeded randomness (Math.random in planners, unpinned sampling) is a reproducibility bug filed against the harness, not bad luck.

blocks.caption: Seeded randomness injected and logged: replay proven, not hoped

blocks.text: Dry runs: full logic, stubbed effects

**Dry-run mode** executes the complete loop with side effects replaced by stubs (recorded responses or declared fakes): logic verified without touching the world. Refactors prove safe in dry-run before touching production; new branches tested against recorded gold responses. Dry runs that diverge from live behavior indicate stub drift — refresh recordings, don't abandon the mode.

blocks.caption: Stubs record calls; unstubbed access fails loudly (coverage proof)

blocks.text: Checkpoints plus replay enable **forks**: resume from step N with edited state ('what if approval differed?'), run forward, compare outcomes. Forks answer counterfactuals that logs alone can't: which decision caused the failure, and what would the alternative have done? Production incidents get forked in staging; fixes proven on forks before deploy.

blocks.title: Prove determinism
blocks.note: Run it: expect true, true, plus the deterministic sequence. Same seed → identical choices, different seeds diverge: replay proven by construction, and unseeded Math.random would fail the first assertion.

items: Log inputs + seeds + spans + tool responses: replay proven by test (same → identical)
Dry runs stub effects, execute logic fully; unstubbed access fails loudly (coverage proof)
Forks from checkpoints answer counterfactuals; fixes proven on forks before deploy

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice determinism proof and record the trial-42 sequence. (b) Replace mulberry32 with Math.random in runTrial and state which assertion breaks (and why that breakage is the whole point). (c) Write the dry-run stub map for a refund flow (lookup + issue tools) with one recorded response each.
hints: Baseline: identical-true, differs-true, plus the fixed sequence (record it — replay means same forever).
Math.random breaks same-seed-identical (unseeded nondeterminism): the assertion that proves replay now fails — demonstrating why planners must inject seeded RNGs.
Stubs: lookup → recorded order row; issue → recorded receipt; unlisted tools throw (coverage proof).
exercise.why: Breaking determinism on purpose (Math.random swap) proves the requirement negatively: replay needs seeded injected randomness, and the failing assertion is the detector. Stubs complete the sandbox.
exercise.code: // Determinism-proof pattern: same-seed equality asserted in CI.

quiz.q: Same inputs, different traces across runs. First suspect?
options: Unseeded randomness or unlogged inputs (live tool responses, Math.random in planners) — reproducibility inputs missing
quiz.explain: Nondeterminism has exactly two sources: unlogged inputs and unseeded randomness. Both are harness gaps, fixed structurally (seeds + cassettes).

quiz.q: Dry run passes, production fails. Likely gap?
options: Stub drift: recorded responses stale vs live behavior — refresh recordings; the mode is sound, the fixtures aged
quiz.explain: Stubs are snapshots: live APIs evolve past them. Refresh cassettes on schedule/failure; divergence indicts fixtures, not the pattern.

quiz.q: 'What if approval differed at step 4?' Answer how?
options: Time-travel fork: resume from checkpoint 4 with edited approval, run forward, compare — counterfactuals by construction
quiz.explain: Checkpoints + replay enable forks: alternative histories executed, not imagined. Fixes proven on forks before deploy.

summary: Seeded inputs, recorded responses, dry-run sandboxes, checkpoint forks. Reproducibility designed in, proven by test, wielded via time-travel.
next: Reproducible runs need enforced boundaries: validation layers, approval hooks, and audit trails. Next: guardrails in the harness.
